task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR hard gate (WF-02 Step 1b) on REQ-197's design (lib/letflow/design/req197-expr-arithmetic-and-errors.md, queue task 370, GH#716). REQ-197 extends lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex (shipped, REQ-050/REQ-111, S3) with arithmetic (+ - * / %), unary negation, and a structured parse-error surface, while EE-05's contract (transition.ex's evaluate_condition/2 call collapsing any failure to false) must stay byte-for-byte intact and expr.ex's grep-verified zero-impurity contract must keep returning zero matches. Read docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-197 entry in full yourself before validating -- do not trust this summary alone. Note the design's own §0 states R-Co's real src/expr source tree (ast.zig/lexer.zig/error.zig/evaluator.zig) is NOT reachable from this sandbox (confirmed by filesystem search, no *.zig file anywhere on this host) -- every semantic rule in the design is therefore taken from the requirement text's own quoted restatement of R-Co's source, not from independently reading R-Co directly, and the design flags 4 explicit open questions (§12, OQ-1..OQ-4) about details the requirement text under-specifies (signed-infinity/NaN split for float div-by-zero, the comparison-null 'yields null' reading, no eval-time structured-error surface, and negative-operand integer div/mod rounding direction) rather than silently guessing them. Check whether this flagging is adequate rather than a cop-out -- in particular OQ-4 (negative-operand int / and % rounding) and OQ-1 (signed infinity) are real, currently-untested assumptions baked into concrete @spec/table content elsewhere in the design (§4.3), not deferred blank slots -- confirm the design is still internally consistent and buildable even though these two specific numeric edge cases are unverified against real R-Co source.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of REQ-197's 12 real acceptance_criteria (read from docs/requirements.yaml, not from this handoff) maps to a concrete design element -- verify the design's own §11 traceability table against the actual requirement text yourself rather than trusting the table.

Zero literal Elixir implementation code anywhere in the design doc -- grep the file for 'defmodule', 'def ', and a trailing bare 'end' outside a @type/@spec continuation; confirm every fenced block is a @type/@spec declaration, a comment-only pseudocode sketch, or a BNF/table, never a working function body.

The extended ast() type (§2) and precedence table (§2.1) actually match the requirement text's stated precedence verbatim: loosest to tightest is or, and, not, comparison, + -, * / %, unary -, primary -- check the parser call-graph diff (§3.1) implements exactly this chain with no level skipped or misordered.

The arithmetic semantics table (§4.2/§4.3) matches the requirement text's stated rules exactly: int+float promotes to float; int div-by-zero and int mod-by-zero are errors; float div-by-zero yields IEEE infinity; float mod-by-zero is always an error (not just on zero divisor -- check the design says 'always', matching the requirement text's unconditional framing); and confirm the null asymmetry (§4.5) is stated as its own explicit, separately-tested rule, not folded silently into the type-mismatch generic case.

The structured parse-error type (§6.2/§6.3/§6.4) genuinely carries line, column, offending token text, and a message field, and the design specifies a real mechanism for populating line/column (not zero-by-construction, which is the exact defect the requirement calls out in R-Co's own EvalError) -- verify §6.2's line/column bookkeeping description is concrete enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without further judgment calls.

The two-entry-point boundary (§6.1/§6.6) is unambiguous: parse/1's existing @spec and outer {:error, {:parse_error, reason}} shape is explicitly unchanged (checked against the one existing wildcard-reason test this design cites at expr_test.exs:157), parse_strict/1 is new and separate, and evaluate_condition/2's source is stated as requiring zero edits -- confirm this reasoning is sound, not just asserted, by checking whether any existing test in test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs pins parse/1's error-reason shape more specifically than a wildcard (if one does, the design's backward-compatibility claim in §6.1/§0 is wrong and this must FAIL).

Purity re-verification (§7) names the exact grep command from expr.ex's own moduledoc and explicitly calls out every new code surface (arithmetic eval clauses, infinity-sentinel construction, position-tracking tokenizer, describe_parse_error/1) that must be covered by it -- confirm none of these new surfaces has an obvious purity leak the design failed to flag (e.g. does the line/column bookkeeping in §6.2 risk any clock read, any process dictionary use, anything beyond pure string/integer bookkeeping?).

The now()/date_add/date_diff disposition (§8) is a genuine DECIDED disposition with stated reasoning (not added, ever, without a future injected-timestamp mechanism -- clock reads permanently ruled out), not left open, and section 9's moduledoc-content table maps this decision to AC9's exact wording requirement.

Section 10's non-goals list matches the requirement's own NOT-IN-THIS-REQUIREMENT list item-for-item: REQ-198's 8 builtins, CEL macros/collections/ternary/in, benchmark.zig port -- confirm nothing here is broader or narrower than the requirement's actual text.

Confirm the design's claim (§3.2, §9 final paragraph) that none of the 5 new single-character operator tokens collides with or weakens any existing @unsupported_call_markers entry -- spot check this claim against the actual marker list in lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex:59-77 yourself.

CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (this file, top level, not nested under result) must be exactly one of PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish your pass -- grep the file yourself before finishing, and run mix letflow.lint_handoffs if available, per this project's own recurring anti-pattern entry on this exact mistake.

result.summary:
Read docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-197 entry in full (lines 10662-10767), lib/letflow/design/req197-expr-arithmetic-and-errors.md in full, lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex and lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex directly (not from the design's description of them), and test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs. Most of the design is sound and independently re-derivable: AC1-4 and AC6-12 each map cleanly to a concrete design element (checked the §11 traceability table row-by-row against the requirement's 12 actual acceptance_criteria, not the count); the precedence table (§2.1) matches the requirement's verbatim order (or, and, not, comparison, + -, * / %, unary -, primary) with no level skipped, confirmed against the real parse_or->parse_and->parse_not->parse_cmp->parse_operand chain at expr.ex:314-381; the arithmetic semantics table (§4.2/§4.3) matches int+float promotion, int div/mod-by-zero-is-error, and float mod-by-zero-is-always-an-error (the design's table correctly says 'always', matching the requirement's unconditional framing) verbatim; the two-entry-point boundary (§6.1/§6.4/§6.6) is sound -- confirmed expr_test.exs:157 really is the only parse/1 error-reason assertion and it really is a wildcard `_reason` (lines 156-158), so parse/1's outer shape can stay unchanged and parse_strict/1 can be added as a pure sibling; confirmed transition.ex has exactly one Expr call site (evaluate_conditioned_edges/3, transition.ex:670-671) and its comment (654-660) matches the design's EE-05 framing, so the zero-edit claim for evaluate_condition/2 is structurally sound, not just asserted; the purity grep command (§7) is copy-pasted verbatim from expr.ex's own moduledoc (expr.ex:29-33) and the new-surface coverage list is concrete; the now()/date_add/date_diff disposition (§8) is a genuine decided-with-reasons disposition, not left open; §10's non-goals list matches the requirement's NOT-IN-THIS-REQUIREMENT list item-for-item; spot-checked @unsupported_call_markers (expr.ex:59-77) and confirmed none of the 16 entries contains +, -, *, /, or % as a substring; grepped the whole design doc for 'defmodule', 'def ', bare 'end' -- zero matches, every fenced block is a @type/@spec/BNF/table, no implementation code.

BLOCKER (OQ-2 is not a genuine open question -- the requirement text already answers it, and the design's disposition contradicts that answer): design §4.5/§12 OQ-2 treats 'null in a comparison still yields null' as satisfiable by the *existing, unchanged* eval/2 behaviour -- i.e. an ordering comparison with a nil operand keeps producing {:error, {:eval_error, {:type_mismatch, op, lv, rv}}} (expr.ex:437-446, is_number(lv) and is_number(rv) guard, unchanged), and the design argues the requirement's 'yields null' phrase is satisfied only at the evaluate_condition/2 catch-false boundary (an error collapses to false the same as any other error). But docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-197 description states this in the SCOPE section, not as an ambiguous aside: 'Note the deliberate asymmetry Letflow must preserve: null in a COMPARISON propagates (yields null), but null in ARITHMETIC is an error.' This is an instruction to make eval/2 itself return {:ok, nil} for a nil operand in an ordering comparison -- not a restatement of the already-shipped, already-erroring behaviour. AC5 confirms this is not satisfiable by the design's reading: 'null in a comparison still yields null and null in arithmetic yields an error -- the deliberate asymmetry, asserted as two explicit tests.' Under the design's own §12 OQ-2 disposition, BOTH cases (comparison-with-null and arithmetic-with-null) still produce an {:error, {:eval_error, ...}} tuple from eval/2 today -- there is no asymmetry left to test at the eval/2 level (both collapse to false identically at evaluate_condition/2, indistinguishably), which directly contradicts AC5's demand for two tests that demonstrate two DIFFERENT outcomes (a value vs. an error). This is exactly the class of gap WF-02 Step 1b's check 2a exists to catch: a MUST/AC with no design element that actually satisfies it. Verified this is safe to fix (not blocked by any shipped test): grepped test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs for 'nil'/'null' -- zero matches, so no existing test pins today's type_mismatch-on-nil ordering-comparison behaviour; changing it is unconstrained by any shipped assertion.

Disposition of the other 3 open questions (§12), since routing back for OQ-2 alone would otherwise leave these unresolved: OQ-1 (signed infinity/NaN 3-way split, §4.3) and OQ-4 (negative-operand int div/mod truncate-toward-zero direction, §4.2 row A) are both genuine, real external-fact gaps -- R-Co's actual src/expr/evaluator.zig is independently confirmed unreachable from this sandbox (no *.zig file anywhere on this host), and neither the requirement text's single unsigned phrase ('yields the IEEE infinity') nor its silence on negative operands resolves either one; no acceptance criterion in docs/requirements.yaml tests the 0.0/0.0 NaN case, the signed-infinity case, or any negative-operand div/mod case. OQ-1 is the riskier of the two: it bakes new machinery (a 3-variant infinity_marker() type, new value()/ast() surface, new comparison-ordering branches in §4.6) into concrete @spec/table content on the strength of the design's own reasoned guess, untested by any AC, purity-adjacent (a new sentinel-construction code path §7 must cover) -- this should be carried to REVIEWER for explicit sign-off before ELIXIR-DEV builds on it, mirroring how REQ-191's global-table divergence and REQ-192's INV-RT-1 resolution were escalated rather than silently decided. OQ-4 is lower-risk: it reuses Elixir's native div/2 and rem/2 semantics with no new type or AST surface, is the common C-family/Zig-heritage convention, and is safe to proceed with flagged for REVIEWER's awareness rather than blocking. OQ-3 (no eval-time structured-error surface) is not really an open question at all -- the requirement text only asks for a structured PARSE-error surface (SCOPE item 3), never an eval-time one, so §6.6 point 3's scoping-out is already the requirement's own answer, not a guess; no rework needed on this point, just noting it is mislabeled as an OQ.

issues.description: §4.5/§12 OQ-2: the design leaves eval/2's ordering-comparison null handling unchanged (still {:error, {:eval_error, {:type_mismatch, ...}}} for a nil operand, per expr.ex:437-446), reading REQ-197's 'null in a comparison propagates (yields null)' as satisfied by the evaluate_condition/2 catch-false boundary alone. The requirement text states this as a scope instruction to preserve/implement, not an ambiguous aside, and AC5 requires two tests demonstrating two DIFFERENT eval/2-level outcomes (comparison yields a value, arithmetic yields an error) -- unsatisfiable under the design's current disposition, since both cases still produce an error tuple today. Fix: revise §4.2 to add an explicit null check ahead of the existing is_number guard in the ordering-comparison eval clause (and state whether this also covers eq/neq, where nil==nil/nil==5 already behave sensibly via plain Elixir ==) so a nil operand in an ordering comparison returns {:ok, nil} rather than a type-mismatch error; update §4.5's asymmetry table accordingly; update §11's traceability row for AC5. No existing test in test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs pins today's nil-ordering-comparison error behaviour (grepped for nil/null: zero matches), so this change is unconstrained by any shipped assertion.

result.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER -- 1 BLOCKER above (OQ-2 mislabeled as unresolvable when the requirement text already answers it), rework iteration 1. Carry forward OQ-1 (flag for explicit REVIEWER sign-off before ELIXIR-DEV implementation) and OQ-4 (safe reasoned default, flag for REVIEWER awareness only) unchanged into the reworked design; OQ-3 needs no change, just re-labelling as a scoped-out non-question rather than an open one.
